neuropsychological improvement is associated with favorable outcome in patients with schizophrenia, schizoaffective, and mood disorders.

neuropsychological dysfunction in schizophrenia and schizo-affective disorder is associated with poor psychosocial outcome and that improvement in psychosocial outcome is associated with neuropsycho- logical improvement.

the presence of neuropsychiatric dysfunction in schizophrenia and mood disorder patients is associated with unfavorable psychosocial outcome at a 2-year evaluation, and that neuropsychological improvement may require a period of psychosocial stability, in schizophrenia and major mood disorder syndomes.

the relationship between neuropsychological performance and psychosocial outcome, and suggests that the latter may be a function of the former, in the course of the recovery of schizophrenia and major mood disorders.

the role of neuropsychological dysfunction in the etiology and treatment of psychiatric illness.

neuropsychological deficits are associated with poor outcome in the short term, whereas the reverse is true in the long term.
neuropsychological deficits may be an end result, rather than a cause, of poor outcome in psychiatric disorders.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
neuropsychological improvement may require a stable period for a favorable psychosocial outcome in schizophrenia and schizo-affective disorder, as in major mood disorder syndomes.
the presence of neuropsychologic deficits is associated with poor outcome in schizophrenia and schizo-affective disorders.
cognitive deficits are a major factor contributing to outcome in schizophrenia, and to a lesser extent in major affective disorders.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cognitive impairment in psychiatric illness does not appear to be static, and may change with clinical course.
the relationship between cognitive dysfunction and poor clinical outcome in psychiatric illness is not a simple one.
neuropsychological improvement is not necessarily associated with a favorable clinical course.
